title: Azure Logic Apps Overview
description: Build low-code integration workflows with Logic Apps triggers, actions, connectors, and run history.

data.text: Logic Apps is Azure's workflow engine for integration. You define a trigger (what starts the workflow) and a series of actions (what happens next), and the platform runs and monitors each execution. It ships with hundreds of connectors for services such as Office 365, Salesforce, Service Bus, SQL Server, and Blob Storage, which is why it is often faster than writing custom integration code.

data.caption: A Logic App starts with a trigger, evaluates conditions, and calls connector actions; every run is recorded for debugging.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    TRIG["Trigger\nevent or schedule"] --> WF["Logic App workflow"]
    WF --> COND{"Condition"}
    COND -->|true| ACT1["Action: call connector\nor HTTP endpoint"]
    COND -->|false| ACT2["Action: log and stop"]
    ACT1 --> NEXT["Next actions"]
    ACT2 --> HIST["Run history"]
    NEXT --> HIST
    HIST --> MON["Monitor and replay"]

data.text: A Logic App is a JSON document with `triggers` and `actions`. Actions reference the output of earlier steps with expressions such as `@triggerBody()` and `@body('Parse_order')`. A Consumption Logic App is defined by one workflow; a Standard Logic App can host many workflows in a single resource.

data.title: HTTP request trigger with a condition
data.content: Orders above 1000 route to an approval email. The `runAfter` property controls sequencing when actions depend on each other.

data.title: Deploy with the Azure CLI
data.content: The `logic` CLI extension creates a Consumption workflow from a definition file.
data.code:
az logic workflow create \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --name la-order-processor \
  --location westeurope \
  --definition workflow.json

data.title: Run history is the debugging tool
data.text: Every Logic App run records the input and output of each action. When an integration fails, open the run history, find the failed action, and inspect its inputs — that is usually faster than adding logging. For production, also enable diagnostics to Log Analytics so you can alert on failure counts.

data.title: Interview angle: Logic Apps is integration, not application code
data.text: Logic Apps is the right tool when the work is orchestration: connect systems, transform a payload, wait for approval, retry on failure, and keep an audit trail. It is the wrong tool when the work is a long-running service with complex business logic, high request volume, or custom algorithms. In those cases you write a Function or a service and let the Logic App orchestrate the calls.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Logic Apps is a low-code workflow engine for integration between systems.
A workflow is a JSON document with triggers and actions.
Connectors provide prebuilt operations for hundreds of services.
Consumption Logic Apps are serverless and pay per execution; Standard Logic Apps run in a dedicated environment.
Run history records every trigger and action input and output.
Use Logic Apps for orchestration and Functions for custom code.
